  - text: S1
  - heading "Summary" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Operations profile for India covering road-freight cost and emissions structure, the PM e-DRIVE electric-truck scheme, BEE draft fuel-efficiency regulations, the Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines, and the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 port-capacity and shore-power targets.
  - text: S2
  - heading "Substantive findings" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Operational cost baseline
  - paragraph: This profile synthesises current intelligence on operational costs, regulatory environment, infrastructure feasibility, and the road-freight decarbonisation landscape for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in India. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with air and road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with India serving Asia-Europe and Asia-Americas trade lanes plus significant domestic road-freight legs.
  - paragraph: SCOPE
  - paragraph: Transport accounts for 14% of India’s GHG emissions, with medium and heavy-duty trucks responsible for 44% of that share—despite comprising just 3% of vehicles on the road.
  - paragraph: India’s logistics costs, at about 13% of GDP, far exceed the global average.
  - paragraph: With 70% of freight moving by road and fuel making up a large portion of costs, electrifying trucks is both an environmental and economic imperative.
  - paragraph: Logistics costs remain high, with companies spending 10–15% of their expenses on transporting goods to and from factories.
  - paragraph: "— \"India's Transport Transformation: Three Policies to Shape the Road Ahead"
  - link "theicct.org":
    - /url: https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/
  - paragraph: "\" ICCT"
  - paragraph: — ICCT
  - link "theicct.org":

    - /url: https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization
  - paragraph: "\" WRI India"
  - paragraph:
    - emphasis: "Per the workspace's reading:"
    - text: both sources independently confirm road freight's outsized cost and emissions footprint in India (70% of freight by road per ICCT; 10-15% of a shipping company's own expenses spent on transport per WRI India), which is the structural reason road-fleet decarbonisation and cost pressure are linked issues for a workspace's Indian road legs, not separate topics.
  - paragraph: SCOPE
  - paragraph: The high upfront cost of electric trucks, coupled with limited charging infrastructure, remains a significant roadblock.
  - paragraph: — WRI India
  - link "wri-india.org":
    - /url: https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization
  - paragraph:
    - strong: Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.
  - paragraph: "GAP: Specific current diesel retail price (INR/litre, national average) is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17."
  - paragraph: "GAP: Specific total-cost-of-ownership breakeven or payback period figures for electric versus diesel trucks in India are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17."
  - paragraph: Feasibility of operational choices
  - paragraph: SCOPE
  - paragraph: India has only 869 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles.
  - paragraph: — WRI India
  - link "wri-india.org":
    - /url: https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization
  - paragraph:
    - emphasis: "Per the workspace's reading:"
    - text: fewer than 900 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles in service nationally is a very small base relative to India's overall truck fleet; electric road-freight capacity is not yet a scaled operational option for the workspace's Indian road legs.
  - paragraph: SCOPE
  - paragraph: In July 2025, the Ministry of Heavy Industries released guidelines for electric trucks under the PM e-DRIVE scheme.
  - paragraph: "By supporting electric trucks, e-DRIVE addresses three challenges at once: Reducing logistics costs through lower fuel dependency. Strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced EV technologies such as heavy-duty batteries and charging systems. Improving air quality along highways and in cities, with health benefits for millions."
  - paragraph: BEE has released draft fuel-efficiency regulations for light-, medium-, and heavy-duty vehicles—regulations with immense potential to reshape the road transport sector.
  - paragraph: the Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines provide a framework to shrink the environmental footprint of ports—targeting over 60% renewable energy use by 2030 and 90% by 2047, electrifying half of port equipment by 2030 and 90% by 2047.
  - paragraph: — ICCT

  - paragraph: ANALYTICAL INFERENCE
  - paragraph: Analytical inference
  - paragraph: the Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines' own renewable-energy and port-equipment-electrification targets are staged out to 2030 and 2047; shore power and port electrification are policy-roadmap items, not yet operationally available at Indian ports at scale, per the captured pool.
  - paragraph: not citable
  - paragraph: LEGAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED
  - paragraph: whether the Harit Sagar Guidelines are binding on port operators, or advisory only, is not established by the captured pool and requires legal confirmation before being cited to a client as a compliance requirement.
  - paragraph: —
  - paragraph: Talking points
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "What the workspace can credibly say:"
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - emphasis: "Per the workspace's reading:"
      - text: road transport is responsible for a disproportionate share of India's transport emissions (medium- and heavy-duty trucks are 44% of transport's GHG share while being only 3% of vehicles on the road) and a disproportionate share of cost (logistics run 10-15% of a shipping company's own expenses, and India's logistics costs overall are about 13% of GDP), which is why electrification and efficiency policy for trucks is a live, high-priority area of Indian government action.
    - listitem:
      - emphasis: "Per the workspace's reading:"
      - text: the PM e-DRIVE scheme (July 2025 guidelines) and Bureau of Energy Efficiency draft fuel-efficiency regulations are both active, named policy instruments the workspace can reference when discussing India's road-freight decarbonisation trajectory with a client.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "What the workspace should not claim without verification:"
  - list:
    - listitem: Do not present electric trucking as an operationally available choice for Indian road freight at any meaningful scale; fewer than 900 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles are in service nationally per WRI India.
    - listitem:
      - emphasis: "Legal Confirmation Required:"
      - text: do not cite the Harit Sagar Guidelines as binding regulation on port operators; their enforcement status is not established by the captured pool.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Questions the workspace can pose to clients:"
  - list:
    - listitem: "\"For your India-origin or India-destination shipments, is diesel fuel volatility or the 10-15%-of-expenses logistics cost burden the client's own team has flagged as the bigger near-term concern?\""

  - paragraph: It envisions expanding port capacity from 2,500 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA) today to more than 10,000 MMTPA, supported by world-class infrastructure, digital innovation, hydrogen and ammonia hubs, carbon-neutral operations, and shore power at all major ports by 2047.
